doc.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021

title: The Fender Rhodes sound and Miles's pedals
summary: He approached the Rhodes for its own colors rather than as a piano, and applied Miles's trumpet pedals to it.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: The sound that you got on the Rhodes and carried you through different recordings, were you hearing that, I mean there was a lot of tremolo, some reverb, some effects. I’m trying to think how to ask this question. When you were recording were you hearing those effects or were they added later?

Oh no. Oh it was right there. What happened was you know that’s why I got kind of upset because I think the Fender Rhodes did a documentary on the Fender Rhodes and I don’t know why they didn’t call. Because Chick and everyone else, and Herbie, they approached the Fender Rhodes the same way you approach the grand piano but you can’t do that. Because the Fender Rhodes is a different color and different sounds. So I was approaching the Fender Rhodes from the sound and the colors that were coming out of the Fender Rhodes. So you can’t play it like — you’re not playing a grand piano. So, and then when I was with Miles, Miles had all these pedals hooked up to his trumpet. So when I got to the Fender Rhodes I said well let me do the same thing Miles did, but I’m going to hook the pedals up to the Fender Rhodes. And Monk, it worked. I came up with, I guess they call it the “Lonnie Liston Smith Cosmic Sound.”
